PROCEDE POUR CALCULER DES PHASES RELATIVES ENTRE DES VOIES DE SIGNALISATION DANS UN DISPOSITIF DE POURSUITE A CAPTEURS MULTIPLES

abstract.p: Disclosed is a method for calculating relative phase between channels of a multi-sensor tracking device. The relative phases may be used to calibrate the multi-tracking sensor device to perform more accurately. The method involves recording a plurality of first signals generated by a first channel of the multi-sensor tracking device. The plurality of first signals are generated during a movement of the multi-sensor tracking device. Typically, the multi-sensor tracking device includes several channels, each one of which includes at least one sensor for sensing movement with respect to a corresponding axis. Concurrent to recording of plurality of first signals, a plurality of second signals generated by a second channel of the multi-sensor tracking device, is recorded. The plurality of second signals are generated during the movement of the multi-sensor tracking device. Thereafter, a relative phase between the first and second channels is calculated as a function of the recorded plurality of first signals and the recorded plurality of second signals.

L'invention concerne un procédé pour calculer des phases relatives entre des voies de signalisation dans un dispositif de poursuite à capteurs multiples. Les phases relatives peuvent être utilisées pour calibrer le dispositif de poursuite à capteurs multiples en vue d'atteindre une plus grande précision. Le procédé consiste à enregistrer une pluralité de premiers signaux générés par une première voie du dispositif de poursuite à capteurs multiples pendant un mouvement dudit dispositif. Le dispositif de poursuite à capteurs multiples inclut généralement plusieurs voies comprenant chacune au moins un capteur pour détecter un mouvement par rapport à un axe correspondant. En même temps que l'enregistrement de la pluralité de premiers signaux, une pluralité de deuxièmes signaux générés par une deuxième voie du dispositif de poursuite à capteurs multiples est enregistrée. La pluralité de deuxièmes signaux est générée pendant le mouvement du dispositif de poursuite à capteurs multiples. Ensuite, une phase relative entre la première voie et la deuxième voie est calculée en fonction de la pluralité de premiers signaux et de la pluralité de deuxièmes signaux enregistrés.

description.p: TITLE: METHOD FOR CALCULATING RELATIVE PHASES BETWEEN SIGNAL CHANNELS IN A MULTI-SENSOR TRACKING DEVICE
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
1 Field of the Invention
The present invention relates to the field of multi-sensor tracking devices, and more particularly to a method of calculating relative phases between channels of a multi-sensor trackmg device
2 Descπption of the Relevant Art

Multi-sensor tracking devices are well known in the art and are used to oπent movmg components of a system employing the device with respect to a known position Multi-sensor trackmg devices have application in, for example, virtual reality systems More particularly, tracking devices may be employed in a headset of a virtual reality system to generate oπentation signals relatmg an instant position of the trackmg device, and thus the headset, relative to a predetermined pomt in space

Fig 1 is a block diagram of a typical multi-sensor trackmg device 12 used to track angular motion Tracking device 12 shown in Fig 1 mcludes three signal channels 14A-14C, respectively, coupled to a digital signal processor 16 Channels 14A-14C include motion sensors 20A-20C, respectively, analog signal processmg circuits 22A-22C, respectively, and analog to digital converters 24A-24C, respectively

Although not shown in Fig 1, each sensor 20A-20C is physically mounted withm tracking device 12 such that a sensitive axis thereof substantially aligns with one of the orthogonal axes of the tracking device 12 More particularly, sensitive axis of sensor 20A is substantially aligned with the azimuth axis, sensitive axis of sensor 20B is substantially aligned with the elevation axis, and sensitive axis of sensor 20C is substantially aligned with the roll axis

In theory, each sensor is sensitive to motion with respect to a smgle axis of the tracking device 12, but insensitive to motion with respect to the remaining axes Thus, if trackmg device 12 shown m Fig 1 is subjected to simultaneous movement with respect to all three of its orthogonal axes, each motion sensor simultaneously generates an analog signal the magnitude of which is linear to the component of movement with respect to its corresponding axis These signals may be proportional to the angular position, angular velocity, or angular acceleration about the given axis

Analog signals generated by motion sensors 20A-20C are provided as mputs to analog signal processmg circuits 22A-22C, respectively Analog signal processmg circuits 22A-22C provide one or more functions In particular, analog signal processing circuits 22A-22C may operate to amplify the sensor analog signal inputted thereto Additionally, analog signal processing circuits 22A-22C may operate to filter random pattern or fixed pattern noise components of the analog sensor signal inputted thereto The processed analog signals are then provided to analog to digital converters 24A-24C for conversion Digital signal processor 16 coordinates function of the analog to digital converters 24A-24C More particularly, digital signal processor 16 generates a sample
signal which is simultaneously received by each of the analog to digital circuits 24A-24C In response thereto, internal sample and hold circuits within the analog to digital converter circuits 24A-24C, sample and hold the analog signals outputted by analog signal processing circuits 22A-22C The held sampled analog signals are subsequently transformed mto digital format by analog to digital converters 24A-24C and forwarded to digital signal processor 16. At this point the relative phases of the three channels are locked, and remain precisely defined throughout the processmg within the digital signal processor

Digital signal processor 16 operates m accordance with well known algorithms to generate an oπentation signal as a function of the three digital signals outputted by the channels 14A-14C in general, and the analog to digital converters 24A-24C m particular. For example, digital signal processor may accumulate digital channel signals representing angular velocity m order to generate onentation signals relatmg current position of the trackmg device 12 to a known start pomt.

It is important to note that the algorithms employed withm digital signal processor 16 may operate to combme data from the three separate channels with the presumption that the channel signals are synchronous However, this is not always the case. Manufacturing tolerances dictate that corresponding elements withm the channels 14A-14C are less than physically identical These physical differences between components may cause relative signal delay between channels Additionally differences between analog signal processmg circuits 22A and 22B may cause a greater signal transmission time through signal processing circuit 22A when compared to signal processmg time through circuit 22B. Thus, analog signal processing circuits 22A and 22B may generate analog signal outputs at different times (i.e., out of sync ) notwithstanding sensor signal mputs provided at the same mstant of time. The overall relative time delay, also referred to as relative phase, between signals outputted by channels 14A-14C, may impair accuracy of the subsequently generated oπentation signals
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present mvention relates to a method for calculating relative phases between channels of a multi- sensor trackmg device The calculated phases can be subsequently used by an internal digital signal processor to generate a more accurate orientation signal The multi-sensor tracking device compnses a plurality of channels each one of which includes at least one sensor for sensing movement with respect to a corresponding axis To calculate at least one relative phase between channels, the trackmg device is subjected to a known movement constrained with respect to one of the orthogonal axes thereof As the trackmg device moves, a plurality of first signals generated by a first channel is recorded. Concurrently, a plurality of second signals generated by a second channel are likewise recorded. Thereafter, a relative phase between the first and second channels is calculated as a function of the recorded plurality of first signals and recorded plurality of second signals. It is this relative phase which may be used to compensate for relative time lags between signals propagatmg through the first and second channels in subsequent real time application of the trackmg device

DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

Fig. 2 shows a schematic diagram of a system for calibrating a multi-sensor trackmg device. More particularly, Fig. 2 shows a relative phase calibration circuit 30 coupled to a multi-sensor trackmg device 32 via a

Trackmg device 32 defines a multiple degrees of freedom onentation trackmg device used to sense motion with respect to multiple orthogonal axes and generate onentation signals relatmg cunent position of the tracking device to a known start pomt. Trackmg device 32 generates orientation signals by analyzmg, comparing or combmmg internally generated signals relatmg to trackmg device movement In one embodiment, trackmg device 32 may sense angular motion with respect to the three orthogonal axes of azimuth, elevation, and roll, and generate internal signals conespondmg thereto In this embodiment, the trackmg device contains an embedded digital signal processor which can calculate the trackmg device's current onentation relative to a known start point by accumulatmg angular velocity of the device with respect to three axes

Relative phase calibration circuit 30 may take the form of a processor based system configured to execute software or firmware. Alternatively it could take form of a different mode of operation of the same digital signal processmg system used m normal operation. As will be more fully descnbed below, phase calibration circuit 30 generally calculates relative phases or signal delays between signals transmitted through channels contamed withm multi-sensor trackmg device 32. The calculated relative phases are then used to calibrate trackmg device 32. Calibrated m this way, trackmg device 32 can compensate fixed, relative system signal transmission delays and thus generate more accurate onentation signals

Fig 3 is a block diagram of one embodiment of the tracking device 32 shown in Fig 2 Trackmg device 32 shown m Fig 3 is configured to sense motion of the device with respect to the azimuth, elevation, and roll axes, and to calculate the device's onentation relative to a known start pomt usmg the sensed motion The onentation may be calculated, for example, by accumulatmg angular velocity in the three axes It is noted, however, that the present invention is not to be limited to application to the multi-sensor tracking device shown m Fig. 3
Multi-sensor trackmg device 32 shown m Fig 3 includes three channels 40A-40C coupled to digital signal processor 41 Each of the channels 40A-40C is configured to generate a channel signal which is lmear in magnitude to a an orthogonal component of motion of tracking device 32 These channel signals are subsequently used by digital signal processor 41 to generate onentation signals Each of the channels 40A-40C mclude motion sensors 42A-42C, respectively, analog signal processmg circuits 44A-44C, respectively, and analog to digital converters 46A-46C, respectively Additional components may be mcluded withm each of the channels 40A-40C However, for purposes of explanation, it is noted that each channel 40A-40C contains corresponding components

Motion sensors 42A-42C may constitute miniature high performance angular sensors which are configured to sense motion along sensitive axes contamed therem Trackmg device 32 is shown with a smgle sensor m each of the three channels 40A-40B Alternatively, there may be multiple sensors associated with each channel 40A-40B or multiple smgle sensor channels associated with each orthogonal axis in order to minimize random pattern noise on the internally generated signals by averaging sensor output m multiple sensor channels or channel outputs in smgle sensor channels aligned to the same axis Further, multiple smgle sensor or multiple sensor channels may be provided to enable a wide range of motion types without compromismg sensitivity between the motion types The present mvention will be descnbed to trackmg device 32 havmg just three smgle sensor channels conespondmg to three orthogonal axes, respectively Although not shown m Fig 3, each sensor 42A-42C mcludes a sensitive axis mounted m substantial alignment with one of the three orthogonal axes of trackmg device 32 Thus, motion sensor 42A has a sensitive axis substantially m alignment with the azimuth axis of trackmg device 32, motion sensor 42B has a sensitive axis m substantial alignment with the elevation axis of trackmg device 32, and motion sensor 42C has a sensitive axis in substantial alignment with the roll axis of trackmg device 32 If trackmg device 32 is subjected to random movement, each sensor, 42A-42C may simultaneously generate an analog sensor signal which is proportional to a component of the movement along the sensor's conespondmg axis These analog signals are provided to analog signal processmg circuits 44A-44C, respectively Analog signal processing circuits 44A-44C may operate to perform any one of a number of functions For example, analog signal processmg circuits 44A-44C may perform sensor signal amplification, sensor signal random pattern noise removal, or sensor signal fixed pattern noise removal The output of the analog signal processmg circuits 44A-44C, still m analog form, are provided to analog to digital converters 46A-46C respectively In one embodiment, the analog to digital converters 46A-46C may mclude internal circuitry (not shown m Fig 3) for samplmg and holdmg signals outputted by analog signal processmg circuits 44A-44C, respectively, in response to a sample signal provided by processor 41 More particularly, the internal sample and hold circuits may be controlled via the sample signal provided by digital signal processor 41 such that each sample and hold circuit withm analog to digital converters 46A-46A, samples and holds analog signals provided by analog signal processmg circuits 44A- 44C at substantially the same instant in tune, or at a known, fixed time delay relative to the other channels, for example multiplexing the mput to a smgle analog to digital converter subsystem The sampled analog signals are ultimately converted mto digital format, the results of which are provided to digital signal processor 41 where they are combmed under control of the processors software to generate the onentation signals

Like the prior art tracking device shown in Fig 1, trackmg device 32 shown in Fig 3 suffers from cross- channel signal lag due to manufacturing tolerances between conespondmg components The relative phases
impacts the ability of the tracking device to generate accurate orientation signals The relative signal delays between channels (or relative phases), however, can be calculated and the tracking device calibrated accordingly as will be described below Given that the relative phases will not generally change with time, the relative phases can be calculated once and stored withm digital signal processor 41 at the factory where the tracking device 32 is calibrated so that subsequent use of trackmg device will result in more accurate oπentation signals

In one embodiment, the relative phases are calculated by first applying a stimulus to one channel (e g channel 40A) of channels 40A-40C of trackmg device 32 In other words, trackmg device 32 is subjected to motion constrained to one axis (e g azimuth) of the three orthogonal axes thereof It is to be understood, however, that relative phases may be calculated by applymg a stimulus simultaneously to two or three of the three channels 40A-40C The present mvention for calculating relative phases exploits cross-axis sensitivities between channels 40A-40C In essence, cross-axis sensitivity causes unexpected signals to be generated m, for example, cross channels 40B and 40C, when a motion stimulus is applied solely to the principle axis associated with channel 40A This unexpected or enor signal is typically due to the fact that the sensitive axes of the sensors are often not conectly aligned with the geometncal axes of the trackmg device, or there is inherent sensitivity withm the detector means to stimuli m orthogonal channels However, this misalignment is fixed and the cross axis sensitivity signals generated are likewise fixed This results m cross axis enor signals on the cross channels that are linearly proportional to the stimuli applied to the one channel Additional sources of cross axis enor can be due to cross coupling between electrical signals of separate channels Agam, this effect is typically linear Alternatively, movement in a plane substantially out of the planes of sensitivity of the three orthogonal axes will also give rise to sets of Imearly proportional signals which can be used for phase alignment However the on-axis method descnbed has the advantage that it is based upon the sort of calibrated motion about smgle axes normally required for accurate channel calibration If signal to noise ratio of cross axis signals is poor, the out of plane measurements could be used m addition to the on-axis method described

As trackmg device 32 is moved solely with respect to the azimuth axis thereof, motion sensor 42A generates a senes of analog signals Additionally, a series of conespondmg analog signals are generated by motion sensors 42B and 42C due to cross axis sensitivity The analog motion signals generated by sensors 42A-42C are subsequently processed by analog signal processmg circuits 44A-44C, respectively Analog to digital converter circuits 46A-46C sample and hold outputs of analog signal processmg circuit 44A-44C m response to a sample command generated by digital signal processor 41 The sampled signals are converted into digital format and stored withm a buffer memory (not shown m Fig 3) of digital signal processor 41 or transmitted directly to relative phase calibration circuit 30 (see Fig 2) via data link 34 for storage therem Accordingly, a sequence of digital channel signals CA-CC, generated in response to movement of the tracking device 32, are recorded for eventual processing by relative phase calibration circuit 30

Relative phase calibration circuit 30executes software that applies an autoconelation function to the recorded sets of channel signals CA-CC m order to calculate relative phases between channels of trackmg device 32 For example, relative phase calibration circuit 30 applies its autoconelation function to recorded channel signals CA and CB generated by channels 40A and 40B, respectively, to calculate a relative phase ΦAB between channels 40A and 40B Relative phase calibration circuit 30 may also apply its autoconelation function to the recorded
channel signals CC-CB to calculate a relative phase ΦCB between channels 40B and 40C and to channel signals CA and CB to calculate a relative phase CAC between channels 40A and 40C

The calculated relative phases ΦAB , ΦBC , and ΦAC may be transmitted back to trackmg device 32 for storage within digital signal processor 41 via data link 34, and subsequently employed to compensate for relative lag m signals transmitted through channels 40A-40C dunng real time use of tracking device 32 However, more accurate relative phases ΦAB , ΦBC , and ΦAC can be provided to tracking device 32 by averagmg results of the autocorrelation function as it is applied to channel signals recorded dunng subsequent movements of trackmg device 32 More particularly, a set of second channel signals CA-CC may be recorded as trackmg device 32 is subjected to movement constrained to the elevation axis, and a third set of channel signals CA-CC may be recorded dunng movement of trackmg device 32 constramed to the roll axis The autoconelation function is applied to the second set of channel signals to generate a second set of relative phases and to the third set of channel signals to generate a third set of relative phases The three sets relative phases can then be averaged to generate average relative phases The average relative phases are subsequently transfened to transfeπed to trackmg device 32 for storage therem where they may be used for real time processmg As noted above, the autoconelation function of relative phase calibration circuit 30 calculates a relative phase between channels usmg channel signals recorded dunng constramed movement of trackmg device 32 with respect to a smgle axis Figs 4A-4F illustrates visually how the autoconelation function calculates relative phases Fig 4A shows wave forms 50A and 50B which represent channel signals CA and CB, respectively, recorded as trackmg device 32 is subjected to movement constrained to the azimuth axis As one might expect, the signals represented by waveform 50B are generated due to cause axis sensitivity Waveforms 50A and 50B have substantially the same shape but are offset m time due to relative phase Figs 4B-4F represent the same waveforms 50A and 50B, but with wave form 50B shifted earlier m time by one time unit (e g , one millisecond) Thus, Fig 4B represents Fig 4A with wave form 50B shifted left by one millisecond, and Figs 4C represents Fig 4B with wave form 50B again shifted left by one millisecond The autoconelation function, in one embodiment, integrates a common area between each normalized waveform 50A and 50B in Figs 4B-4F The intergrations are subsequently compared to identify the largest thereof The largest integration, or an extrapolated version thereof, conesponds to the relative phase For example, Fig 4E shows a common area larger than the common areas m Figs 4A-4D and Fιg 4F Fig 4E represents wave form 50B of Fig 4 A shifted left m time by four milliseconds Thus, with respect to the example shown m Figs 4A and 4F, the relative phase between channels 40A and 40B calculated by the autoconelation function would be close to four milliseconds

Fig 5 is a schematic diagram of a device 60 used in constraining movement of trackmg device 32 with respect to a single axis The device 60 includes a cube 62 configured to be received withm a recess 64 of rotatable plate 66 Cube 60 has at least one face 70 configured to receive trackmg device 32, for example, m the middle thereof The tracking device 32 is mounted to face 70 so that the axes of trackmg device 32 align with faces of the cube 62

With tracking device 32 mounted to cube 62, and with cube 62 received withm recess 64, rotatable plate 66 rotates about its axis and constrains movement of trackmg device 32 with respect to one axis Fig 5 illustrates motion of tracking device 32 constramed to the azimuth axis thereof As rotatable plate 66 travels through a predefined movement (e g , 90 degrees), channel signals generated by the individual channels contained withm
trackmg device 32 are recorded withm an internal buffer of digital signal processor 16 These recorded channel signals are subsequently downloaded to relative phase calibration circuit for relative phase calculation It should be noted that the frequency at which channel signals are generated and recorded, should be sufficiently high to allow an accurate calculation of relative phase The amount of buffer available withm digital signal processor 16 for recording the channel signals and the expected relative time delay between channels, may govern the exact sample rate used For maximum accuracy and minimum buffer space, the recordmg of channel signals may be tnggered by a characteristic stimulus pattern that is known to give strong conelation results (e g , a pulse stimulus to the primary channel)

The process may repeated three time so that three sets of channel signals may be recorded With each process, the cube 62 is removed from recess 64, rotated by 90 degrees, and replaced into the recess Subsequent rotation of rotatable table 66 imparts motion to tracking device 32 that is constramed to a different orthogonal axis An advantage of this approach is that the relative phase data can be gathered at the same time as the calibration required to determine the gam of each axis

Fig 6 is a flow chart illustrating operational aspects of the present mvention to calculate relative phase between channels of the multi-sensor trackmg device shown m Fig 3 At step 104, once the trackmg device is activated for operation, an orthogonal axis is selected Thereafter, the trackmg device is moved about the selected axis as shown m step 106 Channel signals CA-CC generated by channels 40A-40C, respectively as the trackmg device is moved, are recorded as shown m step 108 In step 110, the recorded channel signals CA-CC are provided to the relative phase calculation circuit to calculate relative phases between channels 40A-40C usmg the autocorelation function described above As noted above, it may be preferable to calculate average relative phases from several sets of relative phases, each set bemg calculated usmg a set of channel signals recorded dunng movement of the tracking device with respect to a distinct axis To this prefened end, a decision is made m step 112 as to whether relative phases have been calculated from channel signals generated dur g movement of the trackmg device in all three primary axes thereof If relative phases have been calculated with respect to movement m all three orthogonal axes, then average relative phases are calculated In step 114, the average phases are provided to trackmg device 32 for subsequent use therein However, if a set of relative phases conespondmg to each orthogonal axis has not been generated, the process returns to step 106
